title: Represent Three-Dimensional Figures in Two Dimensions
objective: I can find the surface area of a solid by using its net.
model: net of a prism or pyramid that folds without overlap, faces read off the net and added

widgets.component: fresh problems drawn from a pool: surface area of boxes, cubes, no-lid trays, wrapping-paper sheets, 'which solid folds from 2 triangles and 3 rectangles', faces of a pyramid net, picture of a net
widgets.root: The lesson's idea is the net: a flat pattern that folds into a solid, whose faces are measured. The studio (noAct: true in data/practice-studio/5-6.json) has no widget in which a net is unfolded, folded or built; seven of the seven §4 slots are static multiple-choice, number, table, sort and match items, and the net appears only as a picture (valid cross-shaped nets, checked in studio-viz-geo.js netView). The question 'does this flat pattern fold into a box?' is asked once, in Challenge 4.4, as multiple choice.
widgets.replacement: Build act kind 'netfold' (assets/studio-act/netfold.js, registered in the catalogue, params {solid:'rect-prism'|'cube'|'tri-prism'|'sq-pyramid', dims, goal:'surface'}), reusing the geometry of engine/components/net-folder.js. The student gets three candidate flat patterns (a 1 × 6 strip, a cross, an offset 'T') drawn from the same viz netView with every rectangle labelled by its dimensions; a Fold button animates each flap through 90° and stops at the first overlap, naming the two faces that collide; the student keeps the pattern that folds, then taps each face to read its area off the net and enters the total. Traps to build in: a strip of six rectangles overlapping (Challenge 4.4), counting only the three visible faces, not doubling a pair (Practice 3.3), a missing lid on a tray (pool 11-12). Levels: 1 closed box, 2 cube and no-lid tray, 3 triangular prism (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 4 square pyramid (1 square + 4 triangles). Use it in Practice §4.7 (L2) and Challenge §3.1-3.2 (L3, L4); keep five of the pool items for the other §4 slots.

widgets.component: Connect check: 'What is the surface area of the box?' and 'How many sheets of wrapping paper do you need?' (now carried with the Connect scenario text and the Connect diagram)
widgets.root: The scenario is now shown, but the figure is the Connect bar chart (bars Top & Bottom 280, Front & Back 168, Left & Right 120 with show:true): the bars print the three doubled face-pair areas, whose sum is the answer to item 1, so the work is done on screen. A bar chart is also not a picture of the solid or figure the questions are about. The item is answered by reading the chart.
widgets.replacement: Do not carry a bar-chart diagram into the Mastery section (diagramToViz should return null for kind 'bar-chart', or set show:false until after the answer is checked). Attach instead the net of the box: {"t":"prism","l":14,"w":10,"h":6,"unit":"in","labels":true,"net":true}, and show the bars only in the explanation after the student answers.

widgets.root: The last column compares a number of cubic units with a number of square units. 'Numerically larger' has no mathematical meaning across different units, no reasoning is required beyond reading two numbers, and it does not use a net.
widgets.replacement: Replace column 4 with 'Surface area of the cube whose edges are twice as long' and ask for 24 → 96, 150 → 600, 600 → 2400; add a closing mc 'By what factor did the surface area grow when every edge doubled?' (key 4; distractors 2, 6, 8) so the table teaches scaling, the real idea of that row.
